ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $OABC$ is a rectangle, with point $A$ in the third quadrant. The point symmetrical to point $A$ with respect to $OB$ is point $D$. Points $B$ and $D$ are both on the graph of the function $y=-\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{x}$ $(x<0)$. $BE\perp y$-axis at point $E$. If the extension line of $DC$ intersects the $y$-axis at point $F$, and when the area of rectangle $OABC$ is $6$, what is the value of $\frac{OF}{OE}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect BF and DO,\\
due to symmetry and the properties of rectangles, it's easy to see that $\triangle OAB \cong \triangle BCO \cong \triangle BDO$,\\
$\therefore$BO$\parallel$DF,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle BFE} = S_{\triangle BDO} = \frac{1}{2}S_{\text{rectangle} OABC} = 3$,\\
Moreover, since point B lies on the graph of the inverse proportional function $y = -\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{x}$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle BEO} = \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{OF}{OE} = \frac{S_{\triangle BFE}}{S_{\triangle BEO}} = \frac{3}{\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}} = \boxed{\sqrt{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, the y-axis is vertical upward, and the x-axis is horizontal to the right. Rectangle OABC is tilted to the left, A is in the third quadrant, B is in the second quadrant and on the curve, and C is close to the left side of the y-axis; diagonal OB has been drawn. Point D is near above B and C, also on the curve, and is the symmetric point of A with respect to OB. Through B draw a horizontal line to the y-axis, with foot E; after line DC is extended, it intersects the y-axis at F, and in the figure F is above E. Reasoning: Connect OD and BF. Because D is the symmetric point of A with respect to OB, and O and B are on the axis of symmetry OB, △OAB and △ODB are congruent. Also because OABC is a rectangle, diagonal OB divides the rectangle into two congruent triangles, so △OAB and △BCO are congruent. Therefore △BDO and △BCO are congruent, and it can be obtained that DC (and its extension line DF) is parallel to OB. Since D and F are on the same straight line parallel to BO, △BDO and △BFO take BO as the same base, and the corresponding heights are equal, so the areas are equal. The area of rectangle OABC is 6, and △BDO is half of the rectangle area, therefore S_{△BDO}=3, hence S_{△BFO}=3. Let B=(x_B,y_B). B is on y=-3√2/x and x_B<0, so |x_B y_B|=3√2. E is the foot from B to the y-axis, therefore the area of △BOE is |x_B y_B|/2=3√2/2. △BFO and △BOE both take the segments OF and OE on the y-axis as bases, and the height from B to the y-axis is the same, so S_{△BFO}/S_{△BOE}=OF/OE. Thus OF/OE=3/(3√2/2)=√2.
